title: CS Quest 1.3 · If this, then that (Conditionals and events)
name: If this, then that (Conditionals and events)
summary: Students make Bolt decide for itself, then join conditions with AND, OR and NOT. In Robo Route the fog hides the path ahead, every gem sits on a corner, and from level 3 the layouts change on every run, so only a rule that checks at every step works. An if inside a loop solves any maze. One device per student.
iCan: combine conditions with AND, OR and NOT and say when the rule is true
nest an if inside a loop so Bolt checks at every step
tell an if (asks now) from a when (waits for an event)
materials: If-Hat printable (a paper hat band, if cards, when cards, AND / OR / NOT joiner cards)
doNow: If it rains at recess, then ___. Now write one rule with AND in it and one with OR in it, about today.
plan: Explore: fog on level 1, the event on level 2, AND on the board

warmup.why: two retrieval items from 1.2, one vocabulary item, one preview of today, one more from 1.2

do: Open Robo Route at Conditionals & events on the projector (Open game at this chapter). Level 1 has fog: Bolt cannot see whether the path ahead is open. Run a plain list of forward blocks first; Bolt bumps. Then build repeat 8 with if / else inside: if path ahead, forward; else, turn left. Run it. Open level 2 and add when gem, turn right above the loop.

On the board write the door rule from the warm-up in English: the door opens if Bolt has the key AND is touching the door. Draw a two-column table, key yes/no against touching yes/no, and fill in which of the four boxes opens the door. Only one does.
say: A conditional lets the program choose. An if asks a question about the world right now; a when listens for something to happen and runs right then.
Two questions can be joined. Wall ahead AND on a gem is true only when both are true. Wall OR paint is true when either is. NOT flips an answer.
ask: Bolt has the key and is two squares from the door. Does the door open? Say the rule with AND and explain.
explore.afterAsk: No: both parts must be true at the same moment. Point at the table: three boxes say no. Then ask what changes if the rule said OR, and fill in that table too.
explore.bigIdea: A rule can join questions with AND, OR and NOT, and an if inside a loop asks it again at every step.

play.goal: 4 levels, so everyone builds a rule with AND
play.stretch: the chapter, then 3 stars; level 7 adds a key and a door to the maze walker
play.solo: one device per student; levels 1 and 2 are if, else and when; from level 3 the board changes on every run; levels 4 and 5 join conditions with AND, OR and NOT; levels 6 and 7 are one maze walker that solves three mazes, the last one with a key and a door; a neighbor may say the rule in words, never touch your screen
lookFors: OR where AND was needed on level 4: Bolt turns right at every gem, not only at the corner gems
the if placed outside the loop, so the question is asked once at the start and never again
reading NOT path ahead as no path anywhere: say it as the way is blocked
play.misconception: AND is not true when one part is true: wall ahead AND on a gem needs both at the same moment, and OR is the joiner that needs only one.
earlyFinishers: help a neighbor without touching their screen

discuss: Write the level 4 corner rule in English, then as blocks. Which word joins the two questions, and why not the other one?
Level 6: one program solved three mazes. What did it check at every step, and why could a counted list of moves never do that?
showMe: One student runs level 4 on the projector in step mode and reads the compound condition aloud each time it is checked; the class answers true or false.

Also says why that joiner and not the other, or how the if inside the loop made one program fit every layout

hint 1 on level 4 names the two questions to join; read-aloud on
the AND / OR table from Explore stays on the board
stretch: level 7: the key maze, then explain the order of the two ifs inside the loop
rewrite the level 5 rule (NOT path OR paint) without NOT, test it, and say whether it still works on all three boards

unpluggedTwin.title: If-Hat, compound round
materials: one paper hat band per group
if cards (if I clap, hop; if I say blue, sit)
when cards (when the chime rings, stand)
steps: The caller wears the hat and holds one if card. The group follows the rule only when its condition is true. Add the else: if I clap, hop; else, clap back.

Compound round: the caller clips two if cards together with a joiner card. If I clap AND I say blue, sit. If I clap OR I wave, hop. If NOT the light is on, freeze. The group calls true or false before acting.
Add a when card to the hat. It can fire in the middle of any round. Ask: which rules were asked when it was their turn, and which one was listening all the time?
Share: which joiner caused the most mistakes, and what was the mistake?

subPlan: Do Now on paper, 3 minutes: finish If it rains at recess, then ___, then write one rule with AND and one with OR about today.

Play Robo Route, chapter Conditionals & events (Pro), one device each, for 20 minutes. Classes, then the lesson, then Play. If the game asks, the quest code is 3 2 0 0. Goal: 4 levels. No warm-up and no projector needed; playing signed out is fine.
Paper exit ticket: the half-sheet with three questions and the sentence frame. Collect it.

shortPeriod40.discuss: Write the level 4 corner rule in English, then as blocks. Which word joins the two questions, and why not the other one?
shortPeriod40.keep: the exit ticket is never cut; in 5 minutes of Explore skip level 2 and keep the AND table

add: the If-Hat, compound round twin (15 minutes) before Play
the 3-star stretch and level 7 after Play
10 minutes of the Unit 1 review on Brain Board

notes: Events are a condition on the world: the when header sits above the program and can fire at any moment during the run.
Levels marked random run on three seeded layouts, so a fixed list of moves that works once fails on the next board. That failure is the lesson.
Vocabulary beyond the five on the learn card: event, sensor, nested if, if / else.
One device per student at this band; the Standards tab counts each student's own play.

steps.title: Today
steps.body:
Do Now: If it rains at recess, then ___. Now write one rule with AND in it and one with OR in it, about today.

Big idea: A rule can join questions with AND, OR and NOT, and an if inside a loop asks it again at every step.

We will talk about:
- The level 4 corner rule in English, then as blocks. Which word joins the two questions?
- One program solved three mazes. What did it check at every step?

steps.title: Warm-up (live)
steps.body: Five quick questions. Your teacher shows them on the projector or starts them live.

steps.title: Play: Conditionals & events
steps.body:
Goal: 4 levels, so you build a rule with AND. Stretch: finish the chapter, then 3 stars.
If the game asks for a quest code, it is 3 2 0 0.
From level 3 the board changes every run. Say the rule in words before you build it: if ___ then Bolt ___. AND needs both parts true. OR needs one. NOT flips the answer.

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.body: Three quick questions about AND, OR, NOT and an if inside a loop.

steps.title: In your own words
steps.body:
